_meta.description: Wallets of Indian exchanges and Indian-run platforms, each row with the public source that names it. Every row is also in that chain's exchange label file (config.Chain.labels_path) as {exchange, label, type}, which is what the matcher reads; this file records where each came from.
_meta.provenance: Public sources only, read without an API key on 14 Nov 2026. (1) The explorer's own public name tag on the address page (etherscan.io/address/<a>, polygonscan.com/address/<a>), read from the page title; source_date is the page's own 'As at' time. Candidate addresses to look up came from dawsbot/eth-labels @ 14247ba8cf4686b747938248bee34c66089fa9d9 (data/csv/accounts.csv) and brianleect/etherscan-labels @ 923aba72c7e2d0682f7ae6194b6140bd90668dc9 (data/*/combined/combinedAllLabels.json); a candidate became a row only if the explorer page for that chain carries the tag. (2) CoinSwitch's own lists of its major (custodial) wallets, published on its blog on 6 Jan 2023 and refreshed on 27 Jul 2023; the chain is the explorer each address links to. Round 2, read without an API key on 15 Nov 2026: (3) CoinSwitch's third (22 May 2024), fourth (22 Oct 2024, cut-off 22 Oct 2024) and fifth (7 May 2025, cut-off 6 May 2025) proof-of-reserves posts, each with its own list of CoinSwitch's major wallets; a row cites the latest edition that lists it, and its kind names the others. (4) WazirX's own proof-of-reserves page, wazirx.com/proof-of-reserves (Internet Archive copy https://web.archive.org/web/20241111131845/https://wazirx.com/proof-of-reserves): the wallet list that page loads was archived four seconds later (the row's source URL); its first page lists the 30 largest of 242,187 wallets by balance, updated 24 Oct 2024. WazirX's 17 Oct 2024 post says it disclosed about 240,000 wallets with balances in an affidavit filed with the High Court of Singapore in Zettai Pte Ltd's restructuring. Only wallets on chains Exchequer traces were taken.
_meta.not_done: No ownership was inferred: no clustering and no guessing. A Polygon row carries the tag PolygonScan itself shows on that address's Polygon page (Etherscan-family explorers show an address's public name tag on each chain they serve), and only where that page shows Polygon transactions. Pages behind a bot check (bscscan.com, arbiscan.io, Etherscan's label lists, the CoinDCX and ZebPay proof-of-reserves pages) were not read; nothing was done to get past one. Round 2 also tried, and took nothing from: CoinDCX's proof-of-reserves posts (Mar 2023 to May 2024) and CoinGabbar's WazirX and CoinDCX proof-of-reserves pages (which WazirX's Jan 2023 PoR PDF names as where its wallets are listed), through the Internet Archive; the copies came back incomplete, or the page loads its wallet list in the browser only. A direct request to coindcx.com met a bot check and was stopped. No ZebPay, Bitbns, Giottus, Mudrex, Unocoin or BuyUcoin wallet list was found: their proof-of-reserves URLs have no archived copy, redirect elsewhere or are not found. Searches for court orders and ED, police or FIU-IND releases found none that names an exchange's own wallet.
_meta.activity: Every Ethereum and Polygon row's address page showed at least one transaction on that chain (EOA or contract as the page says; a contract is typed contract_wallet). The BSC row was checked on the public BNB Chain RPC (bsc-dataseed.bnbchain.org: no code, nonce 210) and the Tron row on TronGrid without a key (account created 2022-12-27, last active 2025-05-26), both on 2026-11-14. Round 2 rows were checked without a key on 14 Nov 2026 (UTC): on Ethereum, BNB Chain, Polygon and Arbitrum through public RPCs (ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com, bsc-dataseed.bnbchain.org, polygon-bor-rpc.publicnode.com, arb1.arbitrum.io): each has sent a transaction (nonce > 0), holds a balance, or has contract code (typed contract_wallet); on Tron each is an existing account, not a contract, on TronGrid. A listed address with none of these was left out.
_meta.kinds: type is the matcher's wallet type; kind is what the source says the wallet is.
_meta.checked: Each address passes the chain's validator (EIP-55 checksum on the spelling a source published, Base58Check on Tron), appears once, and is on no sanctions, freeze, threat, gambling, router or never-flag token list.
_meta.schema: rows: [{address, chain, exchange, label, type, kind, source, source_date, retrieved_on, published_as?}]
